hypotheses.what_was_discovered: next-bar range after NR7 = 0.711x recent median, t=-49.626
hypotheses.why_interesting: volatility clustering implies compression is a state, not a trigger; breakout entries during compression should underperform
hypotheses.mechanism: range compression persists into the next hour (narrowest-range-of-7 predicts below-median next-bar range); use as a NO-TRADE filter for breakout-style entries
hypotheses.testable_prediction: a breakout rule filtered by 'not in NR7 state' outperforms the same rule unfiltered, net of costs, on validation data

hypotheses.what_was_discovered: gap-fill tendency (t=22.366) conditioned on gap size after unconditioned version proved cost-marginal
hypotheses.why_interesting: cycle-1 failure analysis: median gap 5.1 pips vs 1.1-pip cost left ~0 net; large gaps carry proportionally larger targets for the same fixed cost
hypotheses.mechanism: fade only weekend gaps larger than 8 pips toward Friday close with a 24-bar time stop: condition on target size exceeding cost several times over
hypotheses.testable_prediction: large-gap fade (>8 pips, 24-bar stop) has positive net expectancy on train AND validation

hypotheses.what_was_discovered: P(gap fill within 24 bars) = 0.876 over 386 weekends
hypotheses.why_interesting: positioning unwind after illiquid weekend open; event-based, ~52 trades/year, well-defined target and time stop
hypotheses.mechanism: weekend opening gaps revert toward Friday close within 24 H1 bars (fade the gap at Sunday open, target = Friday close)
hypotheses.testable_prediction: fading weekend gaps with target=Friday-close and 24-bar time stop yields positive expectancy net of spread on validation data

proposed_test.entry: Sunday open bar close, direction opposing the gap
proposed_test.exit: Friday close touched OR 24 bars elapsed

hypotheses.what_was_discovered: streak anti-persistence (t=-7.346) re-tested at 8-bar horizon after 1-bar horizon proved cost-dominated
hypotheses.why_interesting: cycle-1 failure analysis: gross edge positive but < cost at 1-bar horizon; if reversion persists beyond one bar, expectancy scales with horizon while cost stays fixed
hypotheses.mechanism: fade 3-bar streaks and hold 8 bars: amortize the fixed roundtrip cost over a 8-hour reversion swing
hypotheses.testable_prediction: 8-bar streak fade clears cost on train AND internal validation

hypotheses.why_interesting: exhaustion/anti-persistence after consecutive moves; distinct from oscillator-level mean reversion (no indicator threshold involved)
hypotheses.mechanism: after 2 consecutive same-direction H1 bars, the next bar reverses more often than chance (fade the streak, 1-bar horizon)
hypotheses.testable_prediction: fading 2-bar streaks yields positive gross expectancy at 1-bar horizon on unseen dev-internal validation data

proposed_test.entry: at close of 2-th consecutive up(down) bar, enter short(long)

hypotheses.what_was_discovered: streak reversal edge (t=-8.96) x highest-vol session (1.384x range)
hypotheses.why_interesting: same probability edge applied where bar magnitude is largest -> gross effect scales with session range while cost is constant
hypotheses.mechanism: fade 2-bar streaks ONLY during the high-volatility late-NY window (17-21 UTC) where per-bar range is 1.38x average
hypotheses.testable_prediction: streak-fade restricted to 17-21 UTC has higher net expectancy per trade than the unconditioned version

proposed_test.entry: counter-streak after 2 consecutive bars, hour in 17-21 UTC

hypotheses.what_was_discovered: streak reversal (t=-7.35) recombined with volatility persistence (t=+53)
hypotheses.why_interesting: conditioning the probability edge on a persistent state variable concentrates trades where gross effect exceeds cost
hypotheses.mechanism: fade 3-bar streaks conditioned on ELEVATED realized volatility (50-bar vol above its median): streak exhaustion should be stronger when moves are large enough to exhaust
hypotheses.testable_prediction: vol-conditioned streak fade beats unconditioned fade net of costs

proposed_test.entry: counter-streak after 3 bars AND vol50 > median

hypotheses.what_was_discovered: hour-of-day return anomalies with |t|>4.4 in the observation window
hypotheses.why_interesting: persistent intraday flow (fixing/rebalancing) can create clock-driven drift; cheap to test, high refutation value
hypotheses.mechanism: systematic directional drift in specific Asia hours (04 UTC negative t=-6.98, 06 UTC positive t=+4.49): time-of-day flow pattern, trade the hour with the sign
